sentences.text:
Applicant has filed this application under Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the impugned orders dated 7.8.2023 and 28.8.2023 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge/F.T.C.-I,
Prayagraj in Sessions Trial No. 217 of 2019; titled State vs. Inayat Hussain @ Babar, arising out of Case Crime No. 57 of 2019, under Sections 376, 506 IPC, Police Station Kareli, District Prayagraj,
whereby firstly the cross-examination of PW-5 was closed by court order and subsequently the application moved by the applicant-accused for recall of PW-5 for cross-examination was also dismissed.
Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the last prosecution witness namely Balwan Singh being Investigating Officer was examined as PW-5 and the cross-examination of the said witness by the defence was closed by the court order on 7th August, 2023.

He submits that on the said date, the applicant was sick, and therefore, he had moved an application seeking exemption from personal appearance, but the trial court proceeded to pass the impugned order, thereby not only rejected the Inayat Hussain @ Babar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173509437/
1 application for exemption from personal appearance, but also closed the opportunity to cross-examine the said witness.

sentences.text: Learned counsel has further drawn the attention of the Court to the order dated 28th August, 2023 and submitted that later the application moved by the applicant seeking recall of PW-5, for his cross-examination, but the same was also declined.

Learned counsel states that since PW-5 is a material witness and if, the applicant is not allowed to cross-examine him, it would result in prejudice to the applicant, and if, one opportunity is granted to the applicant, the applicant would conclude the cross-examination of PW-5.
At this stage, the prayer is opposed by Mr. Manu Khare, learned counsel representing the opposite party no. 2, who has argued that number of opportunities were granted to the applicant to cross-examine the prosecution witness (PW-5), but on every occasion, an adjournment was sought by the defence counsel.
According to him, the witness is posted at a distance of 200 kms.
from the place of trial, therefore, considering the entire background of the case and the conduct of the applicant, the trial court has rightly closed the cross-examination of PW-5.
However, he fairly states that as the accused is praying only for one opportunity, he does not oppose the said prayer, if, the accused keeps his word.

After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the material on record, this Court finds that the charges against the accused were framed in the year 2019 and the prosecution had consumed nearly four years to examine their five witnesses.

Of course, even if, it is assumed that the applicant has been taking unnecessary adjournments for the purpose of cross-examination of PW-5,
if, an opportunity is not granted to the applicant, it would result in prejudice to him and would violate his right to fair trial.

Thus, the impugned orders are set aside and the applicant is granted one opportunity to cross-examine PW-5, either on the next date of hearing before trial court i.e. 27th February, 2024 or any other date to be fixed by the trial court.

Order Date :- 15.2.2024 Brijesh  Inayat Hussain @ Babar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173509437/
